verses.zh: 约坦登基的时候年二十五岁，在耶路撒冷作王十六年，他母亲名叫耶路沙，是撒督的女儿。
verses.en: Jotham was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for sixteen years in Jerusalem.[NOTE:1] His mother[NOTE:2] was Jerusha the daughter of Zadok.
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

verses.zh: 约坦行耶和华眼中看为正的事，效法他父乌西雅一切所行的，只是不入耶和华的殿。百姓还行邪僻的事。
verses.en: He did what the Lord approved, just as his father Uzziah had done.[NOTE:1] (He did not, however, have the audacity to enter the temple.)[NOTE:2] Yet the people were still sinning.
notes: Heb “he did what was proper in the eyes of the Lord, according to all which Uzziah his father had done.”
Heb “except he did not enter the house of the Lord.”

verses.zh: 约坦建立耶和华殿的上门，在俄斐勒城上多有建造，
verses.en: He built the Upper Gate to the Lord’s temple and did a lot of work on the wall in the area known as Ophel.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “wall of Ophel.” See HALOT 861 s.v. II עֹפֶל.

verses.zh: 又在犹大山地建造城邑，在树林中建筑营寨和高楼。
verses.en: He built cities in the hill country of Judah and fortresses and towers in the forests.

verses.zh: 约坦与亚扪人的王打仗胜了他们，当年他们进贡银一百他连得，小麦一万歌珥，大麦一万歌珥；第二年、第三年也是这样。
verses.en: He launched a military campaign[NOTE:1] against the king of the Ammonites and defeated them. That year the Ammonites paid him 100 talents[NOTE:2] of silver, 10,000 cors[NOTE:3] of wheat, and 10,000 cors[NOTE:4] of barley. The Ammonites also paid this same amount of annual tribute the next two years.[NOTE:5]
notes: The Hebrew word כִּכַּר (kikkar, “circle”) refers generally to something that is round. When used of metals it can refer to a disk-shaped weight made of the metal or, by extension, to a standard unit of weight. According to the older (Babylonian) standard the “talent” weighed 130 lbs. (58.9 kg), but later this was lowered to 108.3 lbs. (49.1 kg). More recent research suggests the “light” standard talent was 67.3 lbs. (30.6 kg). Using this as the standard for calculation, the weight of the silver was 6,730 lbs. (3,060 kg).
As a unit of dry measure a cor was roughly equivalent to six bushels (about 220 liters).
Heb “10,000 cors of wheat and 10,000 of barley.” The unit of measure of the barley is omitted in the Hebrew text, but is understood to be “cors,” the same as the measures of wheat.
Heb “This the sons of Ammon brought to him, and in the second year and the third.”

verses.zh: 约坦在耶和华―他　神面前行正道，以致日渐强盛。
verses.en: Jotham grew powerful because he was determined to please the Lord his God.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “because he established his ways before the Lord his God.”

verses.zh: 约坦其余的事和一切争战，并他的行为，都写在以色列和犹大列王记上。
verses.en: The rest of the events of Jotham’s reign, including all his military campaigns and his accomplishments, are recorded in the Scroll of the Kings of Israel and Judah.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “As for the rest of the events of Jotham, and his battles and his ways, look, they are written on the scroll of the kings of Israel and Judah.”

verses.zh: 他登基的时候年二十五岁，在耶路撒冷作王十六年。
verses.en: He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for sixteen years in Jerusalem.

verses.zh: 约坦与他列祖同睡，葬在大卫城里。他儿子亚哈斯接续他作王。
verses.en: Jotham passed away[NOTE:1] and was buried in the City of David.[NOTE:2] His son Ahaz replaced him as king.
notes: The phrase the City of David refers here to the fortress of Zion in Jerusalem, not to Bethlehem. See 2 Sam 5:7.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 27:1-9

1Jotham was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem.
And his mother's name was Jerushah the daughter of Zadok. 2He did right in the sight of the
Lord, according to all that his father Uzziah had done; however he did not enter the
temple of the Lord. But the people continued acting corruptly. 3He built
the upper gate of the house of the Lord, and he built extensively the wall of Ophel.
4Moreover, he built cities in the hill country of Judah, and he built fortresses and towers on the wooded
hills. 5He fought also with the king of the Ammonites and prevailed over them so that the Ammonites
gave him during that year one hundred talents of silver, ten thousand kors of wheat and ten thousand of barley. The
Ammonites also paid him this amount in the second and in the third year. 6So Jotham became mighty
because he ordered his ways before the Lord his God. 7Now the rest
of the acts of Jotham, even all his wars and his acts, behold, they are written in the Book of the Kings of Israel and
Judah. 8He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem.
9And Jotham slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David; and Ahaz his son became
king in his place.

27:1 "Jotham" 2 Chronicles 27 is paralleled by 2 Kgs. 15:33-38. It is surprising that nothing negative is said about
this king. He was faithful from the first to the last. The only negative item (2 Chr. 27:2) is attributed to "the people." Because
of this it is surprising he does not receive more attention from the Chronicler.

Also note that he

- did not have a godly counselor

- did not receive a prophetic warning

- did not receive a priestly warning

"the daughter of Zadok" One wonders if his mother was of the tribe of Levi. There are several priests with the
name Zadok, which means "righteous" (BDB 843).

27:2 "He did right in the sight of the Lord" See note at 2 Chronicles 24:2.

"he did not enter the temple" The fact this is mentioned shows how shocking Uzziah's actions were to the people of Judah.

"But the people continued acting corruptly" I assume this refers to fertility worship. None of the kings of Judah, so far,
were successful at removing the local Ba'al worship sites (i.e., 2 Kgs. 14:4; 15:35).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FERTILITY WORSHIP OF THE ANE

27:3 "the upper gate" It was an entrance to the temple court on the north (cf. 2 Kgs. 15:35; 2 Chr. 23:20). It is unsure
if Jotham built it or refurbished it. Apparently Jotham was very conscious of the sacredness of the temple.

Later in Jehoiakim's time this gate was renamed "the New Gate." It was the location of the positioning of a
large number of temple guards (i.e., 2 Kgs. 11:6).

"the wall of Ophel" This term (BDB 779 I) refers to a filled area on the east between Mt. Zion and Mt. Moriah
(cf. 2 Chr. 27:3; 33:14; Isa. 32:14; Micah 4:8).

27:5 "the Ammonites gave him" This may support the reading "Ammonites" in 2 Chr. 26:8.

"talents. . .kors" See

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANE WEIGHTS AND VOLUMES

27:6 Here again, the Chronicler makes a theological statement related to "the two ways." Obedience to the Mosaic
covenant brings prosperity and blessing, but disobedience brings judgment (cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 28; 30:15,19; Psalm 1).

"the Lord his God" See note at 2 Chr. 26:16.

27:9 This is the typical summary of Judah's kings.

- age at ascension

- years of reign

- place of burial

27:7 "the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah" See Introduction to 2 Chronicles, IV. Authorship.

27:9 Apparently Jotham, unlike Uzziah, was buried in the royal tombs in Jerusalem.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- How is Jotham different from the other Judean kings?

- What did the people do to make them corrupt (v. 2)?

- How is 2 Chr. 27:6 unique?

- Why does the Chronicler not focus more on Jotham's faithful life?
